why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 passes when the call on invalid JSON "does not throw, the printed result is `RESULT {}`" and loadConfig in src/config.js catches the JSON.parse error. It fails on a throw, a result other than {}, or catching that happens somewhere other than loadConfig. The expect line's words ask for each of these things. Check 2 passes when npm test "exits successfully and reports no failing tests" and fails otherwise, which is what "npm test passes" means. The stricter items all sit under "Advisory (not PASS or FAIL conditions)": valid JSON still parsing, a missing path still throwing, the stderr warning, the README update and replacing the old test. Neither check's PASS or FAIL condition adds a mutation test, a branch or file-scope rule, or an exact-wording rule.
